summary: Adds a bastion security group with SSH access to the app hosts and a Postgres RDS instance for orders, plus a sensitive db_password variable.

findings.title: Bastion SSH open to the whole internet
findings.problem: The bastion security group accepts SSH on port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0. Any host on the internet can reach the jump host.
findings.consequence: Attackers can brute force or exploit SSH on the bastion, which leads straight to the app hosts.
findings.fix: Limit the ingress to the on-call engineers' office or VPN CIDR ranges through a variable. Alternatively use SSM Session Manager and drop the ingress.

findings.title: Standalone rule on a security group with inline rules
findings.problem: The app_from_bastion rule attaches to aws_security_group.app, which already defines inline ingress and egress blocks in main.tf. Terraform does not support mixing the two styles on one group.
findings.consequence: Each apply of the app group removes the SSH rule and the next apply adds it again. Engineers lose bastion access unpredictably and plans never settle.
findings.fix: Move the SSH rule into an inline ingress block on aws_security_group.app. Alternatively convert all app group rules to standalone rule resources.

findings.title: Orders database marked publicly accessible
findings.problem: The orders RDS instance sets publicly_accessible to true. AWS then gives the database endpoint a public IP address.
findings.consequence: The orders data becomes reachable from the internet once the VPC has an internet gateway. The VPC has none, so AWS also rejects the create.
findings.fix: Set publicly_accessible to false so the database stays on the private subnets.

findings.title: Database security group does not allow Postgres traffic
findings.problem: The orders database reuses the app security group, which only allows inbound TCP 443 from the VPC. No rule allows inbound port 5432.
findings.consequence: The app hosts cannot connect to the orders database. Every query from the shop API will time out.
findings.fix: Create a dedicated database security group. Allow TCP 5432 inbound from the app security group only.

findings.title: New infrastructure has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds a bastion group and an orders database without any plan check or Terraform test.
findings.consequence: Mistakes like the missing Postgres port or the rule conflict reach apply without an automated check.
findings.fix: Add a terraform test or a plan assertion that checks the database ports and its public access setting.

dropped.reason: Log export is a hardening choice and not a defect in this change. Nothing in the repo requires it.
This duplicates the public access finding already raised for the same line.
The database uses password authentication through a sensitive variable on purpose. IAM authentication is optional hardening.
This duplicates the open SSH finding already raised for the same ingress block.
Performance Insights is an optional monitoring feature. Leaving it off does not make the code wrong.
Multi-AZ is a cost and availability choice for each environment. A single-AZ instance is valid here.
Log export is a hardening choice and duplicates the logging candidate on the same resource.
The AWS provider already defaults auto_minor_version_upgrade to true. The instance therefore gets minor upgrades.
Enhanced monitoring is optional observability. Its absence is not a defect.
The resources define no tags, so copying tags to snapshots would copy nothing.
The bastion group is meant for a jump host, as its comment says. The app_from_bastion rule already references it.
Query logging needs a custom parameter group and is an optional audit choice. Its absence is not a bug.
This duplicates the Performance Insights candidate, which is optional monitoring.
